nodes.label: Depth-Res-Based GPU Routing (L40S/A100/H200)
nodes.rationale: depth_res determines the GPU tier for video_depth: 714/1078 run on L40S, 1442 landed on A100-SXM4-80GB (slower and pricier), 1806 routes directly to H200 (faster and cheaper than the A100 tier).

nodes.label: Estimate vs Billed Cost Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Estimates ($4.02, timings x Modal pricing) count only per-job stage seconds and are the right tool for COMPARING variants; the billed hour ($6.92) additionally includes a cancelled concurrent attempt, container cold-start/idle (scaledown_window), and the billing poller, so estimate < billed is expected. Billing API lags real-time.

nodes.label: Depth Resolution vs Quality/Cost Tradeoff
nodes.rationale: Subjective quality rises with depth_res: d714 low(3), d1078 low(4), d1442 mid(6), d1806 high(7-8). d1442 was slower/pricier only because it routed to A100-SXM4-80GB while d1806 used H200 directly. Higher output res (1800p/2160p) helps on high-res AVP screens; d714@2160 looks good but may ghost and lose 3D effect.

nodes.label: Auto-Reuse of Preprocess/Depth/Splat Cache
nodes.rationale: Later variants reused the first job's preprocess + depth + 4K splat cache automatically (no job id needed), skipping the depth pass for ~4x speedup; only the inpaint fill differed, giving identical geometry across A/B arms.

nodes.label: Dual-Res Splat (4K detail, 720 hole fill)
nodes.rationale: 4K output keeps sharper real detail while disocclusion holes are filled at 720 either way; the 2b M2SVid@4K run validated the previously-untested dual-res path with no OOM.

nodes.label: ProPainter Flow-Fill Inpainter
nodes.rationale: Cleaner silhouettes with mild flow-fill smear in holes; no hallucinations; rated best (8-10) in subjective A/B tests but ~3x slower than M2SVid.

nodes.label: M2SVid Diffusion Inpainter
nodes.rationale: ~3x faster than ProPainter but introduces hallucinations/ghosting: white fuzz along high-contrast disocclusion stripes at 512-tier working res, milder at qhd. Levers: higher work res or the no_full_attention checkpoint variant. Native right-eye-only; both-eye needs the mirror trick.

nodes.label: DA3 Depth Model
nodes.rationale: Needed two fixes: per-scene alignment anchored to the scene's FIRST frame with a scale guard (chained alignment collapsed to flat gray) and p0.5/p99.5 percentile normalization (min-max was crushed by outlier frames).

nodes.label: DA3-Metric Depth Model
nodes.rationale: Gives consistent cross-scene disparity (job-wide p1/p99 range) but showed a model failure predicting the closest dancer as far (solid black) — a model error, not pipeline overflow; relative mode is immune. Still used internally by the adaptive depth-script profiler for analysis keyframes only.

nodes.label: Depth Pro Profiler/Backend
nodes.rationale: Depth Pro as a depth backend stays on branch depth-pro-backend, unmerged; but it serves as the per-shot profiler (profiler: depth-pro) in v3 adaptive depth scripts.

nodes.label: Horizontal-Mirror Trick for Both-Eye M2SVid
nodes.rationale: M2SVid is a left-reference model; the left eye is synthesized by horizontally mirroring so the same model can be reused. Verified genuinely synthesized (mean |diff| vs pristine = 12.9; a stale-container run showing 0.89 was passthrough). Costs ~2x single-eye (239s vs 133s). Text/logos would mirror-degrade most.

nodes.label: v3 Class-Based Fixed Displacement Scheme
nodes.rationale: In v3 each shot class carries a fixed displacement and placement pair: wide=0.0085/(-1.0,-0.2), standard=0.01/(-1.0,0.3), close_up=0.008/(-1.0,0.1), dynamic=0.009/(-1.0,0.1). Simple, but ignores absolute median depth, causing far-shot over-displacement that v4 later fixed.

nodes.label: v4 Continuous Displacement Ramp by Median Depth
nodes.rationale: Displacement becomes a continuous function of median depth in meters (2m->0.010, 5m->0.008, 11m->0.006, 20m->0.0045 floor), applied per-shot AND per dynamic-keyframe; shot class now sets placement only. Fixes far-shot over-displacement (dance first shot at 14.9m was 0.007 flat, now ~0.0053).
nodes.norm_label: v4 continuous displacement ramp by median depth

nodes.label: v5 Continuous Near-Plane Placement (near_plane_range)
nodes.rationale: v5 job records replace the fixed per-class placement upper values with continuous depth-derived near-plane values reported as near_plane_range (e.g. -0.0294..0.6 for K9); placement upper bound now varies per shot with median depth instead of the fixed class table, on top of the v4 displacement ramp.

nodes.label: Adaptive Per-Shot Depth Script v2 (pro treatment)
nodes.rationale: v2 pro treatment adds depth-matched cuts (placement shifted so convergence feels continuous across scene cuts, unlike v1 which re-centered the depth budget each cut), a comfort budget with clamp flags, capped close-up pop-out (placement upper <= 0.1), and dynamic-shot per-keyframe ramps. Each *_depth_script.json is the per-shot decision log with an adjustments list naming every intervention.

nodes.label: ProPainter Stereo Conversion Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Production pipeline stages visible in job timings: preprocess -> profile_scenes -> chunked video_stereo[propainter] (both-eye inpainting, VDA depth) -> encode_outputs -> encode_mvhevc_x265; outputs sbs + mvhevc, audio muxed from source.

nodes.label: v3 Depth Pro Profiler (true-meters + FOV modifier)
nodes.rationale: v3 classifies shots in TRUE metric meters (close <3m / wide >11m) with per-shot mean horizontal FOV as a modifier (long lens <30 deg biases close-up, wide lens >60 deg biases wide). Depth Pro runs only as a 3-keyframe-per-shot profiler; VDA stays the main depth pass. Device verdict: v3 > v2 because classification accuracy at the source improved (long-lens close-ups correctly called close_up past the 3m metric cut); auto_comfort was a no-op since v3 already lands disparities in-budget.

nodes.label: Silent-Hang Heartbeat Watchdog
nodes.rationale: A letterbox depth job (9d759002879a) hung silently ~94 min with no progress and had to be cancelled/resubmitted; this motivated the ShotProfiler decouple (branch profiler-decouple) and a heartbeat-watchdog follow-up that cancels workers after no progress (later batch failures show 'no worker progress for 600s (silent hang) - cancelled and failed; resubmit').

nodes.label: Depth Reuse Across Tuning Batches
nodes.rationale: Depth maps are reused from the v2 depth-source jobs across tuning batches because displacement/placement tuning does not change depth; v5 extends this to cross-workspace reuse (depth_reused_cross_workspace). Saves the expensive depth pass on every re-tune.

nodes.label: v7 Dual-Resolution 4K Splat
nodes.rationale: Splat (warp) runs at native output resolution (3840x2160) while inpainting runs at a cheap low resolution (1280x720): ~95% of the frame is real warped 4K detail and only disocclusion holes at depth edges carry upscaled-from-720 fill. Stereo GPU routed by splat pixels (H200 at splat_px=8294400, no OOM); frame counts match between splat and work streams so AV sync holds; output 7680x2160 true 4K SBS. ProPainter path GPU-verified and ready to merge; M2SVid path implemented but not 4K-tested; default path byte-identical.

nodes.label: Content-Addressed Preprocess Auto-Reuse
nodes.rationale: Preprocess artifacts are keyed by a deterministic content-addressed hash (same request -> same key, e.g. preprocess:db2b36a02a49...); an identical request auto-reuses preprocess and scene-cut results with no job id passed, skipping preprocess and scene detection entirely. The dual-res splat surface is also published and registered for reuse.
